analysis.investment_thesis: Supertech EV is a 2022-vintage micro-cap (INR 54 Cr) in the hyper-competitive 2W EV / e-rickshaw space with a near-zero 0.47% ROE — the "story" is just a hot-sector label, not a business. Without visible earnings growth, margin data, or scale, the 8.21 P/E is optically cheap but meaningless; there's no PEG math that makes this work.
key_strengths: EV tailwind in India's 2W/3W market provides a real TAM backdrop
Promoter holding of 69.31% implies aligned skin in the game
Low absolute P/E of 8.21 leaves room if earnings ever scale
key_risks: ROE of 0.47% signals the business is effectively non-earning today
Tiny 54 Cr cap competing vs Ola, Ather, TVS, Bajaj, Hero — no moat visible
Only 3 years old (incorporated 2022) with zero long-term execution track record
red_flags: Near-zero profitability (ROE 0.47%) makes the P/E unreliable
Zero DII ownership — no institutional validation
No disclosed revenue/earnings growth rate — can't compute PEG
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my GARP lens, every stock needs a simple story I can repeat in two minutes. Here the story is "small Indian EV maker" — that's a theme, not a thesis. A 0.47% ROE on a company that's barely three years old tells me the unit economics haven't been proven, and in 2W EVs the competitive set (Ola Electric, Ather, TVS iQube, Bajaj Chetak, Hero Vida) is brutal and well-capitalized. Micro-caps can be ten-baggers, but only when you see accelerating revenue, expanding margins, and a defensible niche — none of which is visible here.

The 8.21 P/E looks like a bargain, but P/E on a sliver of earnings is a mirage; one bad quarter flips it to a loss. Without growth rates I can't calculate a PEG, and with ROE under 1% the company isn't compounding capital. Promoter holding at 69% is a positive alignment signal, but zero DII participation suggests no serious institution has done the diligence and signed off. I'd want to watch this from the sidelines for 4–6 quarters of audited revenue growth and margin expansion before touching it. Pass.
